newsitem.title: USA: US Treasury - Mexico's economic recovery underway.
newsitem.headline: US Treasury - Mexico's economic recovery underway.

text.p: Mexico's economic recovery is under way although the effects of last year's recession are still being felt, the U.S. Treasury said Tuesday.
"An economic recovery is under way in Mexico, though the effects of the deep recession of 1995 are still being felt," the Treasury said in its monthly report to Congress on Mexico.
The report is provided as part of the Feb. 21, 1995 agreement in which the United States provided financial assistance to Mexico to help it though an economic crisis.

"Monetary and fiscal policy remain solid," the report said about Mexico. "First-half 1996 fiscal results exceeded government targets, and monetary aggregates remain consistent with a path of steady disinflation," the Treasury said.
Mexico's banking system "remains strained," the Treasury said, but "its restructuring is progressing."

Mexico has met all payments to date and has repaid a net $9 billion in outstanding short- and medium-term swaps to the Treasury and Federal Reserve, the Treasury said. Mexico has $3.5 billion in remaining obligations to the United States under the agreement, the report said.

In the banking sector, asset quality remains a concern, Treasury said. The level of nonperforming loans for the entire private banking system was 13.8 percent at the end of July, up from 13.1 percent at the end of June, the report said.
Restructuring in the banking system continues and as of September, banks will be required to report their risk-based capital adjusted to reflect market risk as well as credit risk, the report said.
"This change will move Mexico closer to international regulatory standards, increasing transparency in the system," the Treasury said.
